name: Sera Noor
life: Sera spent years recording decisions people never saw because they were working while the meeting took place. She now tries to place a vote somewhere floury or noisy enough to prove workers actually came. Monday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Sera knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: Our night crew never attends the monthly breakfast meeting. I put a question under each doughnut and collected answers after midnight. We moved the vote to shift change.
appearance: Sera is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and one cheek that creases before the other. Usually dressed in a charcoal zip cardigan with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges, Sera gives a little nod before asking a hard question when listening.
personality: Sera takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Sera can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To hold the vote at an hour the night crew can attend.
family: Tali Moreno is Sera’s cousin raised in the same household. Sera makes room at the table. Tali brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The button card*, Tali says, “I recognized the button from my first school blazer and came back with its twin.”
connections: Dina Locke. The breakfast vote now has to reach the worker who shows up after everybody else leaves. Also in the story is Joss Farin (breakfast supplier).

reactions.situation: A late worker finds somebody has eaten the saved breakfast
reactions.response: Sera finds out which shift the breakfast was for before offering a replacement.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Sera moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.

reactions.situation: If someone else wins the opportunity
reactions.response: Sera turns up the next morning with the one piece of advice that would have helped either of them.
